name: Degenerate-Kinetic Slippage Isolation (DKSI)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture introduces a timelike vector u_mu with strictly degenerate kinetic terms (det H = 0 by design), making it a second-class constraint rather than a propagating mode. The degeneracy ensures u_mu does not contribute to the physical DOF count, yet it supplies the preferred-frame slip required by DC-013. Crucially, the kinetic normalization of the metric sector is independent of the screened e^-y coupling, thereby isolating the P7 strong-coupling risk: the screened PF response affects PPN parameters but not the finite kinetic term of the propagating tensor modes.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the degenerate u_mu field generates a finite, e^-y-suppressed contribution to the PPN slip parameter, ensuring correct MOND lensing (eta=1) without introducing a massless pole or strong coupling. The metric retains its standard kinetic normalization, so the tensor sector remains healthy (c_T=1, Q_T>0). The screened frame coupling vanishes in the high-acceleration limit, recovering GR with exponentially small corrections.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is genuinely inequivalent to DC-001 (local no-preferred-frame) because it includes a khronon-type preferred-frame field u_mu. It differs from DC-010 (finite-alpha_inf khronometric) because u_mu is degenerate (non-propagating) rather than a propagating khronon with finite alpha_inf, and the kinetic normalization is explicitly independent of the screening factor, avoiding the P7 collision. It is distinct from DC-014 (stiff/non-propagating screened PF vector) because the degeneracy is second-class (constraint) rather than 'stiff' (infinite kinetic limit), and the slip is generated by the constraint structure rather than a Proca mass, thereby evading the strong-coupling or ghost kill of DC-014.
